title: Choosing evenweave fabric
subtitle: The single-thread grid fabric stitched over two threads for a fine, even result.
excerpt: Evenweave has single threads running in both directions, unlike Aida's grouped blocks. You stitch over two threads in each direction, which gives a smoother surface and finer stitch definition than Aida at the same effective count.
sourceNotes:
Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776. Fabric types for counted-thread work.
Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), Internet Archive. Evenweave and linen for embroidery.

glossaryTerms.definition: A plain-weave fabric where the warp and weft threads are the same thickness and equally spaced, producing a grid of individual threads. Cross-stitch on evenweave is worked over two threads in each direction.

The standard technique for working cross-stitch on evenweave: each half-stitch spans two warp threads horizontally and two weft threads vertically. Working over two threads on 28-count evenweave produces the same stitch size as 14-count Aida.

content.text: Evenweave fabric has a grid of individual threads rather than Aida's grouped blocks. When you stitch

, the finished stitch size matches Aida at half the thread count: 28-count evenweave stitched over two = 14-count Aida in effective stitch size. The surface is smoother and the finished fabric has a better drape.
25-count evenweave stitched over two threads: effective stitch size matches 12.5-count Aida. A good step up from 14-count Aida for those ready to try evenweave.
28-count evenweave stitched over two threads: effective stitch size matches 14-count Aida. The most popular evenweave count. A 14-count Aida pattern transfers directly.
32-count evenweave stitched over two threads: effective stitch size matches 16-count Aida. Finer detail; needs magnification in some light conditions.

The holes on evenweave are not pre-formed like those on Aida. The needle parts the individual threads on the way through, so the path through the cloth is less distinct. Beginners find Aida easier to count; evenweave becomes intuitive once you can see the individual thread grid.

items.cause: The needle is going over one thread in some stitches and two in others.
items.fix: Count the threads per stitch carefully. Two threads each way for every stitch: no exceptions.

items.symptom: The fabric is hard to count under poor light
items.cause: Individual threads on evenweave are finer and less distinct than Aida squares.
items.fix: Use a daylight task lamp. A magnifier loupe also helps on 28-count and finer.

content.text: Evenweave is the fabric of choice for advanced cross-stitch, Hardanger, and most surface embroidery sampler work. The
principles here apply equally to linen evenweave.
